prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the standing person directly in front of the camera wearer at roughly 0.4–0.8 m in frames 1–3, with the couch behind and to the left at about 1–2 m and the floor extending farther away around it. The person becomes progressively brighter and larger, indicating approach: by frame 4 the torso is approximately 0.2–0.4 m away and occludes most of the room, and in frame 5 it remains extremely close while shifting toward the left side of view. The person’s arm hangs on the right side of their body and appears within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, while the couch and side table remain beyond easy reach; the map makes this depth ordering and rapid distance reduction clearer than RGB alone. Fine boundaries, absolute metre estimates, the bright region along the bottom of frame 5, and distances on the nearly uniform torso surface look unreliable, and depth alone does not reliably show gaze direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a person in frames 1, 4, and 5 and the couch in frames 2–3, confirming that these large adjoining RGB regions are separate foreground and background surfaces. Spatially, the person is in front of the camera wearer and initially near the centre-right, while the couch lies behind them toward the left; the person then expands to fill almost all of frame 4 and the left/central part of frame 5, showing approach and partial movement out of view. The masks show increasing occlusion of the couch, floor, side table, and other room objects, but they do not provide metric distance, facing direction, gaze, or dependable reach information without the RGB and depth context. The output is unreliable because the person is largely missing in frames 2–3, the couch masks absorb or omit nearby objects, and the close-person masks have holes and incomplete boundaries.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only a small magenta hand configuration near the centre-right of frame 3, corresponding to the nearby person’s hand/forearm area at roughly 0.4–0.7 m from the camera wearer and therefore within reach. Its joint geometry gives a little more precise hand location and articulation than RGB alone, but no usable body skeleton appears, so the person’s full posture, facing direction, gaze, relative limb positions, and reach toward other objects cannot be established from this map. Frames 1–2 and 4–5 are blank even though the RGB clearly contains the person, meaning the map cannot represent the observed approach, the close torso occlusion, or the person shifting partly out of view. The detection is especially unreliable under truncation and extreme closeness, and the isolated frame-3 hand may itself be incomplete or poorly localized.
